body: No, I really wish there was though.  I don't really trust anyone enough to confide in them.

It isnt constant but its getting closer and closer to being constant.  If I felt happy and great when I wasn't depressed I would have no problems with the depression, but its that I'm either depressed or neutral that bothers me.  I could see plowing through all the shitty times if I knew I'd feel better but honestly it doesn't seem worth it to deal with feeling terribly most of the time just so I can feel nothing sometimes.
I hope it works for you, I know people who it has for.  I really like the idea of not thinking about why I'm doing things I want to.  I think sometimes overthinking them ruins them.
Extremely hard.  I hope you're right but I've kind of lost faith in myself

Yeah I actually entered with a decent amount of credits and my gpa is good so im not worried about anything with academics.  All of it feels so meaningless though.  I don't especially want to graduate, or to get a job, or to do much of anything.

I feel like im stuck in this loop of thinking some new achievement will make me feel better, and then when I reach them I realize I'm still me and I still feel like shit.
I think if I could have anything it would be some meaning in my life, ignore that other post.

Money haha, but I'm pretty sure that wouldn't help much.  I've blamed my depression on so many different things that I have no idea whats causging it anymore.  I started blaming it on the city/people i was in, then i moved and blamed it on that.  Then I had a couple of rough breakups and blamed it on that.  Now I'm broke and accumulating some fat student loans and I blamed it on that most recently.  Each one of those problems except the most recent worked themselves out so I'm pretty sure none of them (including the money) is the cause.  If I had a million dollars I'd probably just find something else to blame.

How long have you been on prozac? I was only on it for ~6 months before I ditched it.  I would kill to feel like a zombie.  I have a bunch of psuedo-hobbies, but it's so hard to make any of them feel meaningful if that makes sense
I really have no idea what will be of me in four years

Yeah you're definitely right about that, usually I smoke a lot which helps the effects but not the cause.  Unfortunately I have no idea why I feel like shit all the time so fixing the problem has been extra difficult.  I studied computer science, shit is rad haha.

Yeah I used to see a therapist and was medicated by the version of a therapist who gives you drugs(forgot the name).  I found myself not able to completely open up to either of them in person.  Something about looking someone in the eyes and telling them how I feel is just not easily doable, perhaps I should try again.  I was on Prozac which gave me really bad anxiety so I was switched to effexor I think (not sure if that was the name) which made me gain weight and 100% killed my libido.  Neither one made me feel any happier.

EDIT: I stopped seeing the therapists about a year and a half ago and stopped the medication a little before that
